messages.author: 8d0a80872239233d
messages.subject: Diagnostics for removal models
parts:
Dear all,

I am performing removal models on unmarked using the multinomPois() function. I have come to the point of assessing the goodness of my models and, so far, I have been following the indications from Kéry and Royle (2015) with the following code:

fitstats <- function(final_model) {
    observed <- getY(final_model@data)
    expected <- fitted(final_model)
    resids <- residuals(final_model)
    sse <- sum(resids^2)
    chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
    freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
    out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
    return(out)
    }
parboot(final_model,fitstats,nsim=1000,report=1,parallel=T)

However, after consulting this group and reading recent references I found that AICmodavg has implemented a function to assess the goodness of fit of models performed with unmarkedFrameMPois, as I am. Also, I found on this group some specific recommendations regarding the more appropriate use of this function (also because it allows to obtain the c-hat in a pretty forward way). Should I switch to use this function instead of the fitstats?

On the other hand, I haven't found any comment on the inspection of posterior p to evaluate the uncertainty of the posterior abundance estimates, is that not a regular practice?

Thank you all in advance.

Best
Julien





References:

Kéry M, Royle JA (2015) Applied hierarchical modeling in ecology: analysis of distribution, abundance and species richness in R and BUGS. Academic Press, London, United Kingdom

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Diagnostics for removal models
parts:
Hi Julien,

The goodness-of-fit test in AICcmodavg is based on the chi-square
statistic and the parametric bootstrap to estimate c-hat with parboot(
). This is implemented in Nmix.gof.test( ). The fitstats function you
mention computes the chi-square as well as two other fit statistics,
which you can use with a parametric bootstrap to check goodness-of-fit.
Thus, the difference is in the choice of fit statistic and in the
presentation of the output.

Hope it helps,

Marc
